audit_status.source_base: Hebrew Judges / Shoftim Gideon's pursuit, revenge, kingship refusal, ephod, and aftermath narrative, draft aligned later
audit_status.review_note: First-pass draft reviewed for Ephraim conflict de-escalation, Succoth/Penuel refusal and punishment, Zebah and Zalmunna, revenge for brothers, kingship offer/refusal, gold collection, ephod snare, many wives and sons, Abimelech, and post-Gideon relapse.

verses.restored: Men of Ephraim said to him, What is this thing you did to us, not calling us when you went to fight Midian? They quarreled with him strongly.

familiar.text: And the men of Ephraim said unto him, Why hast thou served us thus, that thou calledst us not, when thou wentest to fight with the Midianites? And they did chide with him sharply.

modern.text: Then the men of Ephraim said to Gideon, “Why have you done this to us? Why did you fail to call us when you went to fight against Midian?” And they contended with him violently.

original.text: וַיֹּאמְר֨וּ אֵלָ֜יו אִ֣ישׁ אֶפְרַ֗יִם מָֽה הַדָּבָ֤ר הַזֶּה֙ עָשִׂ֣יתָ לָּ֔נוּ לְבִלְתִּי֙ קְרֹ֣אות לָ֔נוּ כִּ֥י הָלַ֖כְתָּ לְהִלָּחֵ֣ם בְּמִדְיָ֑ן וַיְרִיב֥וּן אִתּ֖וֹ בְּחָזְקָֽה

verses.restored: He said to them, What have I done now compared with you? Are not gleanings of Ephraim better than vintage of Abiezer?

familiar.text: And he said unto them, What have I done now in comparison of you? Is not the gleaning of the grapes of Ephraim better than the vintage of Abiezer?

modern.text: But Gideon answered them, “Now what have I accomplished compared to you? Are not the gleanings of Ephraim better than the grape harvest of Abiezer?

original.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֲלֵיהֶ֔ם מֶה עָשִׂ֥יתִי עַתָּ֖ה כָּכֶ֑ם הֲל֗וֹא ט֛וֹב עֹלְל֥וֹת אֶפְרַ֖יִם מִבְצִ֥יר אֲבִיעֶֽזֶר

verses.restored: Into your hand Divine gave princes of Midian, Oreb and Zeeb; what could I do compared with you? Then their spirit relaxed from against him when he spoke this word.

familiar.text: God hath delivered into your hands the princes of Midian, Oreb and Zeeb: and what was I able to do in comparison of you? Then their anger was abated toward him, when he had said that.

modern.text: God has delivered Oreb and Zeeb, the two princes of Midian, into your hand. What was I able to do compared to you?” When he had said this, their anger against him subsided.

original.text: בְּיֶדְכֶם֩ נָתַ֨ן אֱלֹהִ֜ים אֶת שָׂרֵ֤י מִדְיָן֙ אֶת עֹרֵ֣ב וְאֶת זְאֵ֔ב וּמַה יָּכֹ֖לְתִּי עֲשׂ֣וֹת כָּכֶ֑ם אָ֗ז רָפְתָ֤ה רוּחָם֙ מֵֽעָלָ֔יו בְּדַבְּר֖וֹ הַדָּבָ֥ר הַזֶּֽה

verses.restored: Gideon came to Jordan, crossing over, he and three hundred men with him, weary yet pursuing.

familiar.text: And Gideon came to Jordan, and passed over, he, and the three hundred men that were with him, faint, yet pursuing them.

modern.text: Then Gideon and his three hundred men came to the Jordan and crossed it, exhausted yet still in pursuit.

original.text: וַיָּבֹ֥א גִדְע֖וֹן הַיַּרְדֵּ֑נָה עֹבֵ֣ר ה֗וּא וּשְׁלֹשׁ מֵא֤וֹת הָאִישׁ֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר אִתּ֔וֹ עֲיֵפִ֖ים וְרֹדְפִֽים

verses.restored: He said to men of Succoth, Please give loaves of bread to people at my feet, for they are weary, and I am pursuing after Zebah and Zalmunna, kings of Midian.

familiar.text: And he said unto the men of Succoth, Give, I pray you, loaves of bread unto the people that follow me; for they be faint, and I am pursuing after Zebah and Zalmunna, kings of Midian.

modern.text: So Gideon said to the men of Succoth, “Please give my troops some bread, for they are exhausted, and I am still pursuing Zebah and Zalmunna, the kings of Midian.”

original.text: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר֙ לְאַנְשֵׁ֣י סֻכּ֔וֹת תְּנוּ נָא֙ כִּכְּר֣וֹת לֶ֔חֶם לָעָ֖ם אֲשֶׁ֣ר בְּרַגְלָ֑י כִּי עֲיֵפִ֣ים הֵ֔ם וְאָנֹכִ֗י רֹדֵ֛ף אַחֲרֵ֛י זֶ֥בַח וְצַלְמֻנָּ֖ע מַלְכֵ֥י מִדְיָֽן

verses.restored: Officials of Succoth said, Is palm of Zebah and Zalmunna already in your hand, that we should give bread to your army?

familiar.text: And the princes of Succoth said, Are the hands of Zebah and Zalmunna now in thine hand, that we should give bread unto thine army?

modern.text: But the leaders of Succoth asked, “Are the hands of Zebah and Zalmunna already in your possession, that we should give bread to your army?”

original.text: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר֙ שָׂרֵ֣י סֻכּ֔וֹת הֲ֠כַף זֶ֧בַח וְצַלְמֻנָּ֛ע עַתָּ֖ה בְּיָדֶ֑ךָ כִּֽי נִתֵּ֥ן לִֽצְבָאֲךָ֖ לָֽחֶם

verses.restored: Gideon said, Therefore when YHWH gives Zebah and Zalmunna into my hand, I will thresh your flesh with thorns of wilderness and with briers.

familiar.text: And Gideon said, Therefore when the LORD hath delivered Zebah and Zalmunna into mine hand, then I will tear your flesh with the thorns of the wilderness and with briers.

modern.text: “Very well,” Gideon replied, “when the LORD has delivered Zebah and Zalmunna into my hand, I will tear your flesh with the thorns and briers of the wilderness!”

original.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר גִּדְע֔וֹן לָכֵ֗ן בְּתֵ֧ת יְהוָ֛ה אֶת זֶ֥בַח וְאֶת צַלְמֻנָּ֖ע בְּיָדִ֑י וְדַשְׁתִּי֙ אֶת בְּשַׂרְכֶ֔ם אֶת קוֹצֵ֥י הַמִּדְבָּ֖ר וְאֶת הַֽבַּרְקֳנִֽים

verses.restored: He went up from there to Penuel and spoke to them similarly, and men of Penuel answered him as men of Succoth answered.

familiar.text: And he went up thence to Penuel, and spake unto them likewise: and the men of Penuel answered him as the men of Succoth had answered him.

modern.text: From there he went up to Penuel and asked the same from them, but the men of Penuel gave the same response as the men of Succoth.

original.text: וַיַּ֤עַל מִשָּׁם֙ פְּנוּאֵ֔ל וַיְדַבֵּ֥ר אֲלֵיהֶ֖ם כָּזֹ֑את וַיַּעֲנ֤וּ אוֹתוֹ֙ אַנְשֵׁ֣י פְנוּאֵ֔ל כַּאֲשֶׁ֥ר עָנ֖וּ אַנְשֵׁ֥י סֻכּֽוֹת

verses.restored: He said also to men of Penuel, When I return in peace, I will tear down this tower.

familiar.text: And he spake also unto the men of Penuel, saying, When I come again in peace, I will break down this tower.

modern.text: So Gideon told the men of Penuel, “When I return in triumph, I will tear down this tower!”

original.text: וַיֹּ֛אמֶר גַּם לְאַנְשֵׁ֥י פְנוּאֵ֖ל לֵאמֹ֑ר בְּשׁוּבִ֣י בְשָׁל֔וֹם אֶתֹּ֖ץ אֶת הַמִּגְדָּ֥ל הַזֶּֽה

verses.restored: Zebah and Zalmunna were in Karkor, and their camps with them, about fifteen thousand, all remaining from entire camp of sons of east; fallen were one hundred twenty thousand men drawing sword.

familiar.text: Now Zebah and Zalmunna were in Karkor, and their hosts with them, about fifteen thousand men, all that were left of all the hosts of the children of the east: for there fell an hundred and twenty thousand men that drew sword.

modern.text: Now Zebah and Zalmunna were in Karkor with their army of about fifteen thousand men—all that were left of the armies of the people of the east. A hundred and twenty thousand swordsmen had already fallen.

original.text: וְזֶ֨בַח וְצַלְמֻנָּ֜ע בַּקַּרְקֹ֗ר וּמַחֲנֵיהֶ֤ם עִמָּם֙ כַּחֲמֵ֤שֶׁת עָשָׂר֙ אֶ֔לֶף כֹּ֚ל הַנּ֣וֹתָרִ֔ים מִכֹּ֖ל מַחֲנֵ֣ה בְנֵי קֶ֑דֶם וְהַנֹּ֣פְלִ֔ים מֵאָ֨ה וְעֶשְׂרִ֥ים אֶ֛לֶף אִ֖ישׁ שֹׁ֥לֵֽף חָֽרֶב

verses.restored: Gideon went up by way of tent-dwellers east of Nobah and Jogbehah and struck camp while camp was secure.

familiar.text: And Gideon went up by the way of them that dwelt in tents on the east of Nobah and Jogbehah, and smote the host: for the host was secure.

modern.text: And Gideon went up by way of the caravan route east of Nobah and Jogbehah, and he attacked their army, taking them by surprise.

original.text: וַיַּ֣עַל גִּדְע֗וֹן דֶּ֚רֶךְ הַשְּׁכוּנֵ֣י בָֽאֳהָלִ֔ים מִקֶּ֥דֶם לְנֹ֖בַח וְיָגְבֳּהָ֑ה וַיַּךְ֙ אֶת הַֽמַּחֲנֶ֔ה וְהַֽמַּחֲנֶ֖ה הָ֥יָה בֶֽטַח

verses.restored: Zebah and Zalmunna fled, and he pursued after them, captured two kings of Midian, Zebah and Zalmunna, and terrified all camp.

familiar.text: And when Zebah and Zalmunna fled, he pursued after them, and took the two kings of Midian, Zebah and Zalmunna, and discomfited all the host.

modern.text: When Zebah and Zalmunna fled, Gideon pursued and captured these two kings of Midian, routing their entire army.

original.text: וַיָּנ֗וּסוּ זֶ֚בַח וְצַלְמֻנָּ֔ע וַיִּרְדֹּ֖ף אַחֲרֵיהֶ֑ם וַיִּלְכֹּ֞ד אֶת שְׁנֵ֣י מַלְכֵ֣י מִדְיָ֗ן אֶת זֶ֨בַח֙ וְאֶת צַלְמֻנָּ֔ע וְכָל הַֽמַּחֲנֶ֖ה הֶחֱרִֽיד

verses.restored: Gideon son of Joash returned from battle by ascent of Heres.

familiar.text: And Gideon the son of Joash returned from battle before the sun was up,

modern.text: After this, Gideon son of Joash returned from the battle along the Ascent of Heres.

original.text: וַיָּ֛שָׁב גִּדְע֥וֹן בֶּן יוֹאָ֖שׁ מִן הַמִּלְחָמָ֑ה מִֽלְמַעֲלֵ֖ה הֶחָֽרֶס

verses.restored: He captured a young man from men of Succoth and questioned him, and he wrote down for him officials of Succoth and its elders, seventy-seven men.

familiar.text: And caught a young man of the men of Succoth, and enquired of him: and he described unto him the princes of Succoth, and the elders thereof, even threescore and seventeen men.

modern.text: There he captured a young man of Succoth and interrogated him. The young man wrote down for him the names of the seventy-seven leaders and elders of Succoth.

original.text: וַיִּלְכָּד נַ֛עַר מֵאַנְשֵׁ֥י סֻכּ֖וֹת וַיִּשְׁאָלֵ֑הוּ וַיִּכְתֹּ֨ב אֵלָ֜יו אֶת שָׂרֵ֤י סֻכּוֹת֙ וְאֶת זְקֵנֶ֔יהָ שִׁבְעִ֥ים וְשִׁבְעָ֖ה אִֽישׁ

verses.restored: He came to men of Succoth and said, Look, Zebah and Zalmunna, about whom you taunted me, saying, Is palm of Zebah and Zalmunna already in your hand, that we should give bread to your weary men?

familiar.text: And he came unto the men of Succoth, and said, Behold Zebah and Zalmunna, with whom ye did upbraid me, saying, Are the hands of Zebah and Zalmunna now in thine hand, that we should give bread unto thy men that are weary?

modern.text: And Gideon went to the men of Succoth and said, “Here are Zebah and Zalmunna, about whom you taunted me, saying, ‘Are the hands of Zebah and Zalmunna already in your possession, that we should give bread to your weary men?’”

original.text: וַיָּבֹא֙ אֶל אַנְשֵׁ֣י סֻכּ֔וֹת וַיֹּ֕אמֶר הִנֵּ֖ה זֶ֣בַח וְצַלְמֻנָּ֑ע אֲשֶׁר֩ חֵרַפְתֶּ֨ם אוֹתִ֜י לֵאמֹ֗ר הֲ֠כַף זֶ֣בַח וְצַלְמֻנָּ֤ע עַתָּה֙ בְּיָדֶ֔ךָ כִּ֥י נִתֵּ֛ן לַאֲנָשֶׁ֥יךָ הַיְּעֵפִ֖ים לָֽחֶם

verses.restored: He took elders of city and thorns of wilderness and briers, and with them he made men of Succoth know.

familiar.text: And he took the elders of the city, and thorns of the wilderness and briers, and with them he taught the men of Succoth.

modern.text: Then he took the elders of the city, and using the thorns and briers of the wilderness, he disciplined the men of Succoth.

original.text: וַיִּקַּח֙ אֶת זִקְנֵ֣י הָעִ֔יר וְאֶת קוֹצֵ֥י הַמִּדְבָּ֖ר וְאֶת הַֽבַּרְקֳנִ֑ים וַיֹּ֣דַע בָּהֶ֔ם אֵ֖ת אַנְשֵׁ֥י סֻכּֽוֹת

verses.restored: Tower of Penuel he tore down, and he killed men of city.

familiar.text: And he beat down the tower of Penuel, and slew the men of the city.

modern.text: He also pulled down the tower of Penuel and killed the men of the city.

original.text: וְאֶת מִגְדַּ֥ל פְּנוּאֵ֖ל נָתָ֑ץ וַֽיַּהֲרֹ֖ג אֶת אַנְשֵׁ֥י הָעִֽיר

verses.restored: He said to Zebah and Zalmunna, What kind of men were they whom you killed at Tabor? They said, As you are, so were they; each one like form of sons of king.

familiar.text: Then said he unto Zebah and Zalmunna, What manner of men were they whom ye slew at Tabor? And they answered, As thou art, so were they; each one resembled the children of a king.

modern.text: Next, Gideon asked Zebah and Zalmunna, “What kind of men did you kill at Tabor?” “Men like you,” they answered, “each one resembling the son of a king.”

original.text: וַיֹּ֗אמֶר אֶל זֶ֨בַח֙ וְאֶל צַלְמֻנָּ֔ע אֵיפֹה֙ הָאֲנָשִׁ֔ים אֲשֶׁ֥ר הֲרַגְתֶּ֖ם בְּתָב֑וֹר וַֽיֹּאמרוּ֙ כָּמ֣וֹךָ כְמוֹהֶ֔ם אֶחָ֕ד כְּתֹ֖אַר בְּנֵ֥י הַמֶּֽלֶךְ

verses.restored: He said, My brothers, sons of my mother, they were. As YHWH lives, if you had preserved them alive, I would not kill you.

familiar.text: And he said, They were my brethren, even the sons of my mother: as the LORD liveth, if ye had saved them alive, I would not slay you.

modern.text: “They were my brothers,” Gideon replied, “the sons of my mother! As surely as the LORD lives, if you had let them live, I would not kill you.”

original.text: וַיֹּאמַ֕ר אַחַ֥י בְּנֵֽי אִמִּ֖י הֵ֑ם חַי יְהוָ֗ה ל֚וּ הַחֲיִתֶ֣ם אוֹתָ֔ם לֹ֥א הָרַ֖גְתִּי אֶתְכֶֽם

verses.restored: He said to Jether his firstborn, Rise, kill them. But the young man did not draw his sword, for he feared, because he was still a youth.

familiar.text: And he said unto Jether his firstborn, Up, and slay them. But the youth drew not his sword: for he feared, because he was yet a youth.

modern.text: So he said to Jether, his firstborn, “Get up and kill them.” But the young man did not draw his sword; he was fearful because he was still a youth.

original.text: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר֙ לְיֶ֣תֶר בְּכוֹר֔וֹ ק֖וּם הֲרֹ֣ג אוֹתָ֑ם וְלֹא שָׁלַ֨ף הַנַּ֤עַר חַרְבּוֹ֙ כִּ֣י יָרֵ֔א כִּ֥י עוֹדֶ֖נּוּ נָֽעַר

verses.restored: Zebah and Zalmunna said, Rise yourself and fall upon us, for as the man is, so is his strength. Gideon arose and killed Zebah and Zalmunna, and took crescent ornaments on necks of their camels.

familiar.text: Then Zebah and Zalmunna said, Rise thou, and fall upon us: for as the man is, so is his strength. And Gideon arose, and slew Zebah and Zalmunna, and took away the ornaments that were on their camels’ necks.

modern.text: Then Zebah and Zalmunna said, “Get up and kill us yourself, for as the man is, so is his strength.” So Gideon got up and killed Zebah and Zalmunna, and he took the crescent ornaments from the necks of their camels. Gideon’s Ephod

original.text: וַיֹּ֜אמֶר זֶ֣בַח וְצַלְמֻנָּ֗ע ק֤וּם אַתָּה֙ וּפְגַע בָּ֔נוּ כִּ֥י כָאִ֖ישׁ גְּבוּרָת֑וֹ וַיָּ֣קָם גִּדְע֗וֹן וַֽיַּהֲרֹג֙ אֶת זֶ֣בַח וְאֶת צַלְמֻנָּ֔ע וַיִּקַּח֙ אֶת הַשַּׂ֣הֲרֹנִ֔ים אֲשֶׁ֖ר בְּצַוְּארֵ֥י גְמַלֵּיהֶֽם

verses.restored: Men of Israel said to Gideon, Rule over us, both you and your son and your son's son, for you saved us from hand of Midian.

familiar.text: Then the men of Israel said unto Gideon, Rule thou over us, both thou, and thy son, and thy son’s son also: for thou hast delivered us from the hand of Midian.

modern.text: Then the Israelites said to Gideon, “Rule over us—you and your son and grandson—for you have saved us from the hand of Midian.”

original.text: וַיֹּאמְר֤וּ אִֽישׁ יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ אֶל גִּדְע֔וֹן מְשָׁל בָּ֨נוּ֙ גַּם אַתָּ֔ה גַּם בִּנְךָ֖ גַּ֣ם בֶּן בְּנֶ֑ךָ כִּ֥י הוֹשַׁעְתָּ֖נוּ מִיַּ֥ד מִדְיָֽן

verses.restored: Gideon said to them, I will not rule over you, and my son shall not rule over you; YHWH shall rule over you.

familiar.text: And Gideon said unto them, I will not rule over you, neither shall my son rule over you: the LORD shall rule over you.

modern.text: But Gideon replied, “I will not rule over you, nor will my son. The LORD shall rule over you.”

original.text: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר אֲלֵהֶם֙ גִּדְע֔וֹן לֹֽא אֶמְשֹׁ֤ל אֲנִי֙ בָּכֶ֔ם וְלֹֽא יִמְשֹׁ֥ל בְּנִ֖י בָּכֶ֑ם יְהוָ֖ה יִמְשֹׁ֥ל בָּכֶֽם

verses.restored: Gideon said to them, Let me ask a request from you: each man give me earring from his spoil. For they had gold earrings, because they were Ishmaelites.

familiar.text: And Gideon said unto them, I would desire a request of you, that ye would give me every man the earrings of his prey. (For they had golden earrings, because they were Ishmaelites.)

modern.text: Then he added, “Let me make a request of you, that each of you give me an earring from his plunder.” (For the enemies had gold earrings because they were Ishmaelites.)

original.text: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר אֲלֵהֶ֜ם גִּדְע֗וֹן אֶשְׁאֲלָ֤ה מִכֶּם֙ שְׁאֵלָ֔ה וּתְנוּ לִ֕י אִ֖ישׁ נֶ֣זֶם שְׁלָל֑וֹ כִּֽי נִזְמֵ֤י זָהָב֙ לָהֶ֔ם כִּ֥י יִשְׁמְעֵאלִ֖ים הֵֽם

verses.restored: They said, We will surely give. They spread garment, and each man threw there an earring from his spoil.

familiar.text: And they answered, We will willingly give them. And they spread a garment, and did cast therein every man the earrings of his prey.

modern.text: “We will give them gladly,” they replied. So they spread out a garment, and each man threw an earring from his plunder onto it.

original.text: וַיֹּאמְר֖וּ נָת֣וֹן נִתֵּ֑ן וַֽיִּפְרְשׂוּ֙ אֶת הַשִּׂמְלָ֔ה וַיַּשְׁלִ֣יכוּ שָׁ֔מָּה אִ֖ישׁ נֶ֥זֶם שְׁלָלֽוֹ

verses.restored: Weight of gold earrings he requested was one thousand seven hundred gold shekels, besides crescents, pendants, purple garments on kings of Midian, and chains on necks of their camels.

familiar.text: And the weight of the golden earrings that he requested was a thousand and seven hundred shekels of gold; beside ornaments, and collars, and purple raiment that was on the kings of Midian, and beside the chains that were about their camels’ necks.

modern.text: The weight of the gold earrings he had requested was 1,700 shekels, in addition to the crescent ornaments, the pendants, the purple garments of the kings of Midian, and the chains from the necks of their camels.

original.text: וַיְהִ֗י מִשְׁקַ֞ל נִזְמֵ֤י הַזָּהָב֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר שָׁאָ֔ל אֶ֥לֶף וּשְׁבַע מֵא֖וֹת זָהָ֑ב לְ֠בַד מִן הַשַּׂהֲרֹנִ֨ים וְהַנְּטִפ֜וֹת וּבִגְדֵ֣י הָאַרְגָּמָ֗ן שֶׁעַל֙ מַלְכֵ֣י מִדְיָ֔ן וּלְבַד֙ מִן הָ֣עֲנָק֔וֹת אֲשֶׁ֖ר בְּצַוְּארֵ֥י גְמַלֵּיהֶֽם

verses.restored: Gideon made it into an ephod and placed it in his city, Ophrah; all Israel prostituted themselves after it there, and it became snare to Gideon and to his house.

familiar.text: And Gideon made an ephod thereof, and put it in his city, even in Ophrah: and all Israel went thither a whoring after it: which thing became a snare unto Gideon, and to his house.

modern.text: From all this Gideon made an ephod, which he placed in Ophrah, his hometown. But soon all Israel prostituted themselves by worshiping it there, and it became a snare to Gideon and his household. Forty Years of Peace

original.text: וַיַּעַשׂ֩ אוֹת֨וֹ גִדְע֜וֹן לְאֵפ֗וֹד וַיַּצֵּ֨ג אוֹת֤וֹ בְעִירוֹ֙ בְּעָפְרָ֔ה וַיִּזְנ֧וּ כָֽל יִשְׂרָאֵ֛ל אַחֲרָ֖יו שָׁ֑ם וַיְהִ֛י לְגִדְע֥וֹן וּלְבֵית֖וֹ לְמוֹקֵֽשׁ

verses.restored: Midian was subdued before children of Israel and did not lift its head again; land was quiet forty years in days of Gideon.

familiar.text: Thus was Midian subdued before the children of Israel, so that they lifted up their heads no more. And the country was in quietness forty years in the days of Gideon.

modern.text: In this way Midian was subdued before the Israelites and did not raise its head again. So the land had rest for forty years in the days of Gideon,

original.text: וַיִּכָּנַ֣ע מִדְיָ֗ן לִפְנֵי֙ בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וְלֹ֥א יָסְפ֖וּ לָשֵׂ֣את רֹאשָׁ֑ם וַתִּשְׁקֹ֥ט הָאָ֛רֶץ אַרְבָּעִ֥ים שָׁנָ֖ה בִּימֵ֥י גִדְעֽוֹן

verses.restored: Jerubbaal son of Joash went and dwelt in his house.

familiar.text: And Jerubbaal the son of Joash went and dwelt in his own house.

modern.text: and he—Jerubbaal son of Joash—returned home and settled down.

original.text: וַיֵּ֛לֶךְ יְרֻבַּ֥עַל בֶּן יוֹאָ֖שׁ וַיֵּ֥שֶׁב בְּבֵיתֽוֹ

verses.restored: Gideon had seventy sons going out from his thigh, for he had many wives.

familiar.text: And Gideon had threescore and ten sons of his body begotten: for he had many wives.

modern.text: Gideon had seventy sons of his own, since he had many wives.

original.text: וּלְגִדְע֗וֹן הָיוּ֙ שִׁבְעִ֣ים בָּנִ֔ים יֹצְאֵ֖י יְרֵכ֑וֹ כִּֽי נָשִׁ֥ים רַבּ֖וֹת הָ֥יוּ לֽוֹ

verses.restored: His concubine who was in Shechem also bore him a son, and he placed his name Abimelech.

familiar.text: And his concubine that was in Shechem, she also bare him a son, whose name he called Abimelech.

modern.text: His concubine, who dwelt in Shechem, also bore him a son, and he named him Abimelech. Gideon’s Death

original.text: וּפִֽילַגְשׁוֹ֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר בִּשְׁכֶ֔ם יָֽלְדָה לּ֥וֹ גַם הִ֖יא בֵּ֑ן וַיָּ֥שֶׂם אֶת שְׁמ֖וֹ אֲבִימֶֽלֶךְ

verses.restored: Gideon son of Joash died in good old age and was buried in tomb of Joash his father, in Ophrah of Abiezrites.

familiar.text: And Gideon the son of Joash died in a good old age, and was buried in the sepulchre of Joash his father, in Ophrah of the Abiezrites.

modern.text: Later, Gideon son of Joash died at a ripe old age and was buried in the tomb of his father Joash in Ophrah of the Abiezrites.

original.text: וַיָּ֛מָת גִּדְע֥וֹן בֶּן יוֹאָ֖שׁ בְּשֵׂיבָ֣ה טוֹבָ֑ה וַיִּקָּבֵ֗ר בְּקֶ֨בֶר֙ יוֹאָ֣שׁ אָבִ֔יו בְּעָפְרָ֖ה אֲבִ֥י הָֽעֶזְרִֽי

verses.restored: It was, when Gideon died, that children of Israel returned and prostituted themselves after the Baals and made Baal-berith their god.

familiar.text: And it came to pass, as soon as Gideon was dead, that the children of Israel turned again, and went a whoring after Baalim, and made Baalberith their god.

modern.text: And as soon as Gideon was dead, the Israelites turned and prostituted themselves with the Baals, and they set up Baal-berith as their god.

original.text: וַיְהִ֗י כַּֽאֲשֶׁר֙ מֵ֣ת גִּדְע֔וֹן וַיָּשׁ֨וּבוּ֙ בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וַיִּזְנ֖וּ אַחֲרֵ֣י הַבְּעָלִ֑ים וַיָּשִׂ֧ימוּ לָהֶ֛ם בַּ֥עַל בְּרִ֖ית לֵאלֹהִֽים

verses.restored: Children of Israel did not remember YHWH their Divine, who had rescued them from hand of all their enemies around,

familiar.text: And the children of Israel remembered not the LORD their God, who had delivered them out of the hands of all their enemies on every side:

modern.text: The Israelites failed to remember the LORD their God who had delivered them from the hands of all their enemies on every side.

original.text: וְלֹ֤א זָֽכְרוּ֙ בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל אֶת יְהוָ֖ה אֱלֹהֵיהֶ֑ם הַמַּצִּ֥יל אוֹתָ֛ם מִיַּ֥ד כָּל אֹיְבֵיהֶ֖ם מִסָּבִֽיב

verses.restored: and they did not do covenant loyalty with house of Jerubbaal-Gideon according to all good he had done with Israel.

familiar.text: Neither shewed they kindness to the house of Jerubbaal, namely, Gideon, according to all the goodness which he had shewed unto Israel.

modern.text: They did not show kindness to the house of Jerubbaal (that is, Gideon) for all the good things he had done for Israel.

original.text: וְלֹֽא עָשׂ֣וּ חֶ֔סֶד עִם בֵּ֥ית יְרֻבַּ֖עַל גִּדְע֑וֹן כְּכָל הַטּוֹבָ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר עָשָׂ֖ה עִם יִשְׂרָאֵֽל

translation_notes: Gideon de-escalates Ephraim's anger with humility and honor-sharing, a constructive contrast to his later vengeance against Succoth and Penuel.
Succoth and Penuel refuse aid out of political risk while Gideon's men are weary; Gideon's response becomes torture, tower destruction, and killing. This is revenge, not justice.
The young man from Succoth is compelled into identifying seventy-seven elders/officials; the coercive information-gathering context must not be ignored.
Gideon tries to make his son Jether execute captured kings, but the youth is afraid and does not do it. Children should not be trained into killing to prove maturity.

Gideon verbally refuses dynastic rule and says YHWH will rule, but his wealth, many wives, seventy sons, concubine, and son named Abimelech ('my father is king') expose a practical drift toward kingship.
The gold ephod becomes a religious snare to Gideon and his house; even a victorious leader's memorial object can become spiritually dangerous.
The return to Baal-berith after Gideon's death continues the book's pattern of fragile memory and post-leader relapse.
safety_note: Do not use Judges 8 to justify torture, collective revenge, coercive interrogation, child execution training, trophy wealth, polygynous power accumulation, or sacred objects becoming leader cults. Center de-escalation where it appears, and expose the slide from deliverance into retaliation, wealth, and quasi-royal status.
